verdict.rationale: Cal.com documents an official client-side building kit, Cal Atoms (embeddable React components with a platform quickstart and managed users), that developers integrate into their own apps. The rest of the evidence covers the raw REST API v2, an official CLI and an MCP server, none of which is a general-purpose SDK, and no OpenAPI spec was found at the probed paths. Missing for 10: documented official language SDKs (e.g., TypeScript/Python client libraries) wrapping API v2, a published OpenAPI spec for codegen, and independent hands-on corroboration of SDK use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Use our react atoms to add scheduling to your app
Cal.com offers a v2 REST API, embeddable React components (Cal Atoms), an embed flow, and a hosted MCP server for AI agents.
Find out how to use Cal "atoms" to integrate scheduling into your product.
This allows you to connect your users to Cal and handle their scheduling with atoms.
